rationale: Both independently rediscover the NPU-mirror twin bug (npu_ar_model_runner.py never got the seq_len fix) and touch on the fragility of the async_chunk default, giving them comparable recall against the largely-already-resolved ground-truth thread; Y additionally surfaces the Med issue's resolution via git history (ede3dddf) which X misses entirely. But X is far more precise and actionable: each finding is a single, well-verified technical claim with clear file/line, concrete fix, and a genuine verification trail (ran tests, traced the shipped deploy config), while Y's output is a repetitive, semi-machine-formatted dump with ~5 near-duplicate entries about the same scoping fact and several broken '?:3508' file references that hurt actionability. X's finding #7 (mm_outputs.py hardening around per-request row-count mismatches, e.g. non-prefill span_len>1 producing no codes.audio) squarely engages the multi-batch-axis fragility that PR #4910 later fixed, while Y's related finding is only a docstring-wording nit — so only X hits the latent gap.
